findings.title: poisson() now accepts whole-horizon and composed processes as its base, silently accounting a mechanism no Opaque sampler realizes
findings.claim: 3b22a6af (#850) replaced `_Inner = Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` with `_Inner = DpProcess` and replaced the factory's type match with `isinstance(self.inner, DpProcess)` (_poisson.py:21, :40-46). Any DpProcess is now accepted, including `DpHorizonProcess` subclasses whose PLD covers a complete fixed horizon (`KOutOfT`, `CyclicPoisson`, `BallsInBins`, `BMinSep`) and `Repeated`/`Composed` spines. Nothing at construction or PLD time distinguishes a per-step base from a whole-horizon base, yet the factory docstring still reads 'Returns a single-step process - compose externally with ``* num_steps`` for full-training privacy' (_poisson.py:185) and docs/reference/accounting.md:232 advertises the widening with no caveat ('Plain Poisson accepts any Opaque `DpProcess` as its base mechanism'). The resulting number is a valid bound only for 'draw ONE dataset-level Bernoulli(q) coin per record, then run the entire horizon on the survivors' - a mechanism no shipped Opaque sampler implements (PoissonSampler redraws per step; KOutOfTSampler has no dataset-level coin).
findings.failure_scenario: Executed at HEAD with a freshly built extension: `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.0), k=2, t=100, allocation='block'), 0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5)` is accepted and returns 0.009738873655638745 for the whole 100-step run. The same horizon unamplified reports 1.233938641105668 (127x higher) and the closest realizable per-step reading, `(dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.0), 0.01) * 100).epsilon_at(1e-5)`, is 0.7180658390624926 (74x higher). Before #850 the same call raised `TypeError: poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner mechanism, got KOutOfT` (git show 4b13d82a:.../amplification/_poisson.py, factory `match inner:` arm). A user who follows the documented 'single-step, compose externally' contract and reports 0.0097 (or 0.087 after `* 100`) for a run driven by KOutOfTSampler publishes an epsilon that no Opaque-realizable configuration attains.

findings.fix_sketch: Keep the generalization but gate it: reject `DpHorizonProcess` instances in `Poisson.__post_init__` (they declare `n_steps` and are not per-step releases), and reject `Repeated`/`Composed` unless the caller opts in with an explicit flag naming the 'one dataset-level coin for the whole inner process' model. Document that model separately from the DP-SGD per-step reading, and say which sampler (none today) realizes it. At minimum, `_poisson.py` and docs/reference/accounting.md:232 must state that the base must be a single release drawn afresh under an independent per-step Poisson draw.

findings.title: Generic Poisson transform costs ~4 orders of magnitude of tightness against the external oracle, and the cross-validation tolerances were relaxed 60x-220x to absorb it
findings.claim: 3b22a6af (#850) deleted the analytic `poisson_gaussian_pld` and routed the Poisson-subsampled Gaussian through `poisson_pld` -> `poisson_from_gaussian` -> `disc_dist` -> `project_transformed_atoms` (poisson.rs:24, :45, :233), i.e. it discretizes the Gaussian loss first and then Connect-the-Dots-projects the transformed atoms, instead of evaluating the exact subsampled hockey-stick curve at each knot. The result is still a strict upper bound (verified, see evidence) but ~4 orders of magnitude looser against Google dp_accounting. The same commit relaxed the external-oracle tolerances from a single `ATOL = 1e-6` to `POISSON_EPSILON_ATOL = 6e-5`, `POISSON_ADVANTAGE_ATOL = 1.3e-5`, `POISSON_BETA_ATOL = 2.2e-4` (test_cross_validation.py:51-54) and retargeted the tight 1e-6 assertion onto goldens generated from opaque's own output (`_POISSON_EPSILON_GOLDENS`, asserted at ATOL on :265, :343). The truncated-Poisson sibling kept the analytic curve (truncated_poisson.rs:57-61 only falls back to `poisson_pld` when `p_trunc == 0.0`), so the two Poisson paths now differ in accuracy by four orders of magnitude. The module comment at test_cross_validation.py:55-57 still claims 'opaque and dp_accounting agree to ~1e-9 relative error'.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured by A/B on the test's own 34-point grid, using a fresh HEAD build of the extension and the pre-#850 .so still checked into packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.abi3.so (which still exports `poisson_gaussian_pld`): worst |new - dp_accounting| in epsilon_at(1e-5) = 5.33e-5 (sigma=0.5, q=1e-3, 1000 steps: new 3.2389339 vs old 3.2388806 vs google 3.2388806), whereas worst |old - dp_accounting| = 3.98e-9. Over a wider 108-point sweep the worst relative gap is 5.7e-4 (sigma=4, q=0.25, 5000 steps) and the minimum signed gap is +9.2e-8, i.e. always conservative. beta_at(0.1) moves by up to 2.1e-4 against riskcal and advantage by up to 1.2e-5, always in the conservative direction. Consequence: a future change that loses another 6e-5 of epsilon (or 2.2e-4 of beta) against the oracle now passes the cross-validation suite; the only remaining tight check is against opaque's own committed numbers, which are regenerated whenever they drift.

findings.title: ParallelPoisson inner-mechanism guard added by #850 lives only in the factory, so direct construction and deserialization bypass it and fail later with a self-contradictory message
findings.claim: 3b22a6af (#850) widened `Poisson`'s inner type and compensated by adding a `match inner: case Gaussian() | AdaClip() | NonPrivate()` guard to the `parallel_poisson()` factory (_parallel_poisson.py:131-140). `ParallelPoisson.__post_init__` (:24-38) validates only `num_workers` and `truncated_batch_size`, so the guard is bypassed by direct construction and by `opaque.serialization.from_state_dict`. This contradicts the convention the very same file family documents: `Poisson.__post_init__` carries the comment 'Validate truncation pairing here (not only in the factory) so direct construction and deserialization can't pass an unpaired (truncated_batch_size, dataset_size) ... and fail at PLD time' (_poisson.py:68-72). The deferred error is also wrong: the `case _` arm reports 'ParallelPoisson requires a Poisson inner mechanism, got Poisson' (:93-98), naming the wrapper instead of the unsupported innermost mechanism.
findings.failure_scenario: Executed at HEAD: `parallel_poisson(eps_delta(0.3), 0.1, 2)` correctly raises `InputTypeError: parallel_poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner mechanism, got EpsDelta.` But `ParallelPoisson(inner=poisson(eps_delta(0.3), 0.1), num_workers=4)` constructs successfully, and `from_state_dict(ParallelPoisson(poisson(gaussian(1.0),0.1),4), state_dict(that_object))` restores it successfully. Both then fail only at `.pld()` / `.epsilon_at()` with `InputTypeError: ParallelPoisson requires a Poisson inner mechanism, got Poisson.` A checkpoint written with an unsupported inner therefore reloads without complaint and dies later in the training loop with a message that points at the wrong object.

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_parallel_poisson.py:93-98 `case _: raise InputTypeError(*("ParallelPoisson requires a Poisson inner mechanism, got " f"{type(self.inner).__name__}.",))`
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_parallel_poisson.py:131-140 factory-only guard added by 3b22a6af
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py:68-72 the stated convention that validation must sit in `__post_init__`, not only in the factory

reproduced at HEAD: construction OK -> `ParallelPoisson(inner=Poisson(inner=EpsDelta(epsilon=0.3, delta=0.0), sample_rate=0.1, ...), num_workers=4)`; `from_state_dict` round-trip OK; `.pld()` and `.epsilon_at(1e-5)` both raise `InputTypeError: ParallelPoisson requires a Poisson inner mechanism, got Poisson.`
findings.fix_sketch: Move the `Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` check into `ParallelPoisson.__post_init__`, matching on `self.inner.inner`, and change the `case _` message in `pld()` to name the innermost mechanism (`type(self.inner.inner).__name__`) rather than the `Poisson` wrapper.

clean_areas: Derived the generalized amplification statement from first principles and confirmed it against the cited primary source. For a base pair (P,Q), Poisson-q gives (P_q, Q) = ((1-q)Q + qP, Q); H_gamma((1-q)Q+qP || Q) = q * H_{(gamma-1+q)/q}(P||Q) for gamma >= 1-q and 1-gamma below that, and H_gamma(Q || (1-q)Q+qP) = (1-gamma(1-q)) * H_{gamma q/(1-gamma(1-q))}(Q||P). Each direction is therefore a pure monotone reparametrisation of the SAME direction's hockey-stick curve, so one-sided hockey-stick domination of the base is exactly sufficient - no stochastic dominance needed. Fetched arXiv:2602.17284 (Feldman & Shenfeld, 'Efficient privacy loss accounting for subsampling and random allocation'): Definition of a PLD realization is E[e^-L] <= 1 with f_L(-inf)=0, the dual is f_D(L)(l)=f_L(-l)e^l with atom 1-E[e^-L] at +inf, and the paper states after Theorem 3.3 that 'Lemma 3.2 essentially guarantees that domination is preserved under the subsampling transformation so if L dominates L_{P,Q} then phi_lambda(L) dominates L_{P_lambda,Q}'. The paper's Claim B.2 says stochastic domination is NOT preserved under subsampling/dual - checked that no Opaque call path feeds a poisson_pld output into the random-allocation transform, which is the only transform whose module doc (pld/realization.rs:1-13) requires first-order stochastic dominance; random_allocation_gaussian_pld builds its own analytic NormalLoss and never takes an external PLD.

Verified the REMOVE transform algebraically against the implementation (poisson.rs:311-339). For each base atom (L, m) the code emits loss log(1-q+q e^L) and mass m*((1-q)e^-L + q); substituting A = 1-q+q e^L gives m'(1-e^{eps-L'}) = q*m*(1 - gamma_b e^-L) exactly, the +inf atom maps to q*M_inf, and the dual-residual atom at log(1-q) with mass (1-q)(1-E[e^-L]) is what makes the total mass sum to 1 and makes delta = 1-gamma in the trivial region gamma < 1-q. Verified the ADD transform (poisson.rs:341-355): loss -> -log(1-q+q e^-l) with masses unchanged and the base +inf atom mapped to the finite maximum -log(1-q), and confirmed the output ADD pmf carries infinity_mass == 0, which is correct because P_q = (1-q)Q + qP is never null where Q is positive.

Verified conservatism of the tagged and untagged Gaussian paths numerically against an independent 60-digit mpmath closed form for the subsampled-Gaussian hockey stick (both adjacency directions, derived independently of the repo's formulas). Over sigma in {0.3,0.5,0.8,1.0,1.5,2.0,3.0} x q in {1e-4,1e-3,1e-2,0.05,0.1,0.3,0.6,0.9} x eps in 0.0..5.9 step 0.1 (3360 points x 2 paths) the worst ABSOLUTE under-estimate of delta is exactly 0. A second sweep over discretization in {1e-4,1e-3,1e-2,5e-2}, log_mass_truncation_bound in {-50,-30,-15}, max_grid_size in {1e7,2000,200} found 0 relative under-estimates above 1e-6. Only at negative eps (eps=-0.5, delta~0.39, outside any privacy-relevant regime) does CtD interpolation under-shoot by 7e-8 relative.

Verified conservatism for a non-Gaussian base it now accepts: for eps_delta_pld(e0, d0) with e0 in {0.05,0.3,1,3,10}, d0 in {0,1e-6,1e-3,0.2}, q in {1e-3,1e-2,0.1,0.3,0.7}, over eps in -2.0..6.0 step 0.05, compared delta_at against the exact two-atom transformed support computed by hand (remove support {(log(1-q+q e^e0), (1-d0)(q+(1-q)e^-e0)), (log(1-q), (1-q)(1-(1-d0)e^-e0))} with infinity q*d0; add support {(-log(1-q+q e^-e0), 1-d0), (-log(1-q), d0)}): worst absolute under-estimate 1.3e-8 on a delta of 0.68 (1.9e-8 relative, floating-point level).

Checked the Connect-the-Dots projection in project_transformed_atoms (poisson.rs:233-306) for conservatism: the grid brackets [floor(L_min/h), ceil(L_max/h)] so it covers the whole transformed support; delta at each knot is the exact tail sum of the transformed atoms plus a positive 8*eps*tail_mass buffer and the infinity floor; delta(eps) is convex in e^eps so the piecewise-linear-in-e^eps reconstruction between knots is an upper bound; discretize_from_deltas' cumulative-min pass can only clamp a knot down to a value that still dominates the true (monotone) curve; and the unused `_adjacency` parameter means passing Adjacency::Remove for the ADD pmf is harmless (connect_the_dots.rs:44-49).

Checked the realization repair (poisson.rs:125-224). Moving probability mass to +inf to force E[e^-L] <= 1 raises delta at every eps (including negative eps), so the repaired pair dominates the input; the repair is capped at 3 rounds and fails closed with 'failed to repair PLD realization' otherwise. Confirmed the repair is not needed on the Gaussian fast path: disc_dist rounds every unit of mass UP, and the Gaussian loss N(1/2sigma^2, 1/sigma^2) has E[e^-L] = 1 exactly, so the discretized law has E[e^-L] <= 1 by construction. On the untagged path the repair moves ~1e-8 of mass, producing a delta floor of q*1e-8 (measured 1.5e-10 at q=0.01, sigma=1.1) - below any delta target the library documents. Also checked the only non-conservative branch, the excess-mass removal at poisson.rs:148-172: it is bounded by REALIZATION_MASS_TOLERANCE = 1e-8, it removes only from atoms adjacent to loss 0 (which contribute nothing to delta(eps) for eps above them), and the realistic trigger is the ~5e-16 over-count that Pmf::self_compose creates by adding the full right_tail_budget to infinity_mass (dense.rs:340-345); no measurable delta reduction was observed in any sweep.

Checked that negative_infinity_mass is safe to ignore (poisson.rs:110-124 docstring vs dense.rs:352-360). Pmf::self_compose adds the left Chernoff budget to negative_infinity_mass without removing it from probs, so finite_mass + infinity_mass is <= 1 and the deficit (at most the ~5e-16 actually-truncated left mass) is pushed to +inf by realization_source - conservative, and total mass of the transform output stays 1 to 1e-12 in every case tested (identity, non-private, Gaussian, composed Gaussian x100).

Checked the fft.rs change in the same commit (numerics/fft.rs:195-232), which makes the bounded CIRCULAR self-convolution the preferred strategy whenever circular_fft_len <= alias_free_fft_len/4 rather than only a last resort. Derived that it stays conservative: fft_len >= truncated_len so each window index maps to a distinct residue; only true indices OUTSIDE the Chernoff window alias into the window, and their total mass is bounded by right_tail_budget + left_tail_budget; right-tail mass that aliases to low indices is separately re-added in full as `result_infinity_mass = composed_infinity_mass + effective_right_budget` (dense.rs:340-345), and left-tail mass aliases to the TOP of the window (higher loss), which also raises delta. The new preference is gated on allow_circular_fallback = use_chernoff, so exact (zero-budget) composition still refuses to alias.

Cross-validated composed Poisson epsilon against Google dp_accounting 0.6.0 (use_connect_dots=True, value_discretization_interval=1e-4) on 34 grid points plus a 108-point wider sweep (sigma 0.4-4.0, q 1e-4-0.25, n 100-5000): opaque's value exceeds the reference at every single point (minimum signed gap +9.2e-8), and advantage/beta were checked against riskcal.analysis at 12 points - advantage always >= reference, beta always <= reference. The generic path is therefore conservative in epsilon, delta, advantage and beta.

Checked poisson(poisson(g,q1),q2) self-consistency: the composed pointwise map log(1-q1+q1 e^L) then log(1-q2+q2 e^.) equals the rate-q1*q2 map exactly, and the implementation reproduces it (delta agreement to 1e-9 relative at typical eps; the double transform is uniformly >= the single, as expected from the extra discretization).

Checked the NonPrivate semantics change (test_nonprivate.py now asserts delta == q instead of 1). Derived it independently: for P perpendicular Q, delta_rem(eps) = q for eps >= log(1-q) and delta_add(0) = q, so q-Poisson subsampling of a fully-revealing mechanism really is (0,q)-DP. The new value is tighter and correct, and epsilon_at(delta) still returns inf whenever delta < q.

Checked robustness of poisson_pld: rates 1e-12 through 0.999999, eps_delta bases with delta up to 0.99, composed and truncated-Poisson bases, and a 199-point sweep of q at eps in {0, 0.5, 1.0} - no panics, no errors, and delta_at is monotone non-decreasing in q at every point (0 violations). rate <= 0 and rate >= 1 are rejected (validate_rate); the Python layer separately routes sample_rate == 1.0 to the unamplified inner PLD.

Verified the k-out-of-t sampler/accountant agreement after fc44ec8d (#761) end to end. KOutOfTSampler(allocation='block') assigns each example uniformly to one step within each of k contiguous blocks of size floor(t/k) or floor(t/k)+1, redrawing independently per block (_k_out_of_t.py:117-124, :139-163); the accountant calls epoch_pld(nm, t, k) -> random_allocation_gaussian_pld, which decomposes t into the same (k - t%k) blocks of floor(t/k) and (t%k) blocks of ceil(t/k) and composes their per-block 1-out-of-size PLDs (random_allocation.rs:186-222). Block-size tuples match exactly. The trainer passes the same k, t=n_steps and allocation to both sides (trainer/_dpftrl.py:315-338 and trainer/_dp_trainer.py:4495-4524), and DDP folds the rank into the sampler key over a disjoint shard, which does not change any record's participation pattern.
